column2: Unsupported city yields the 400 path. | Supported city awaits Save before the 200 path. | The OpenAPI codes are declared and runtime route selection is conditional.
The new-place path awaits Save before responding. | The place insert and guarded request-outbox insert share one transaction. | That transaction's commit completes before Save returns.
The conflict-tolerant insert returns an ID only when it inserts. | The request event is generated only for a returned ID, leaving existing places without a second event.
Dashboard waits for the Places HTTP response. | Outbox publication and card projection are separate conditional work; the response does not await projection.
The 503 catch covers fetch and upstream JSON parsing. | A later transport or parse failure can follow an upstream commit, so the 503 proves neither rollback nor absence of the write.
The unsupported city exits before Save. | A supported new place inserts and enqueues. | An existing place takes the no-new-event branch.
The generated place-request payload is bound to the guarded outbox insert. | The publisher and consumer connection depends on selection, channel and delivery, leaving forecast completion contingent.
Find consumes the stored places returned by List and selects a matching ID. | The missing result yields the declared 404.
A found place creates a fresh request ID and awaits enqueue. | The request is inserted and committed in the same local transaction before the declared 202; persistence remains conditional.
The immediate acceptance waits for enqueue. | Publisher, Forecasts work and Dashboard card projection can occur separately; acceptance does not await them.
The 503 catch covers fetch and upstream JSON parsing. | Enqueue can already have committed, so a proxy failure proves neither rollback nor absence of an enqueued request.
The missing-place branch returns before enqueue. | The found branch awaits enqueue and then returns acceptance.

The later refresh guards control generation of a forecast outbox event. | A separate publisher and conditional Dashboard callback can write the card, whose store supplies GET /api/weather. | Each store and broker transfer is conditional, without an observed or fixed global interleaving.
The hosted registration ties RequestPublisher to ExecuteAsync subject to activation. | The loop tests cancellation and delays 1000 ms between ordinary polls.
The publisher selects one locked unpublished request row. | Parsed payload supplies place.id as the weather.place-requested key and the original payload supplies the unchanged message value.
The ProduceAsync await resumes before the published update and transaction commit await. | This local order does not establish remote delivery.
A send can be accepted before the later DB completion fails. | Under rollback/retry and another poll the pending row may produce a duplicate.
The filtered cancellation handler breaks the loop. | The general handler warns and reaches the 1000 ms delay and next poll under normal continuation.
A false ReadAsync exits before send or published mark. | The immediate return also bypasses successful commit on that path.
Invalid parse or validation follows the rejection path. | That path inserts the rejected record and acknowledges before returning, bypassing the regular inbox.
The typed transaction callback uses the inbox insert result to distinguish duplicates. | A duplicate returns from the callback before place upsert and refresh; the inserted path invokes both.

Normal completion through TransactionTemplate precedes ACK, including the duplicate callback return. | An uncaught DB, refresh or transaction failure before ACK skips it; no broker ACK or successful commit is observed.
Fresh cached data exits early. | Fixture and live modes differ; live access needs User-Agent and a future per-place marker blocks provider send.
The per-place in-memory map receives its retry marker before provider send. | A thrown send leaves that marker without a local reset, outside DB rollback and subject to process lifetime.

A cached 304 updates expiry only; 429 sets backoff. | Live success requires 200/203 and accepted body decoding; other statuses fail before persistence. | Successful decoding flows into JSON parsing and forecast validation before forecast and outbox writes.
The fresh-cache return happens before provider work or parsing. | It also bypasses creation of a forecast-outbox event.
The declared fixed delay defaults to 60000 and activation remains conditional. | Selection finds missing or expired forecast rows and passes them into ordered iteration.
The per-place ID indexes nextAttempt and a future marker blocks a send. | The live path assigns now plus 60 seconds before sending.
The per-place in-memory map is written before provider send. | A thrown send leaves its marker without a reset; the per-place catch and DB rollback do not undo this independent state.
Initial selection is outside the per-place catch and its failure escapes that boundary. | A per-place transaction or refresh failure logs FORECAST_RETRY and continues the iteration when permitted.

The cache, fixture/live, User-Agent and per-place backoff guards bound provider access. | Qualified live success decodes and parses JSON, validates the result, and reaches forecast and outbox writes; other responses have their own guards. | Actual persistence stays conditional.
A separate fresh-cache check still applies after selection. | Its return bypasses the forecast_outbox insert.
The declared publish schedule has PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS with default 1000. | Selection takes one pending row using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
The Kafka future must complete within the bounded 10-second wait before the callback marks the row published. | Local future completion does not prove remote consumer work.
TransactionTemplate contains selection, send and mark. | An accepted send before later DB failure permits a repeat or duplicate, without guaranteeing actual delivery or transaction completion.
The empty-row check returns from the callback before selecting the first row, sending or marking.

A future timeout or failure interrupts local completion before a successful mark or commit. | If Kafka already accepted the send and DB completion fails, a later attempt may duplicate it; remote delivery remains unknown.

The declared topic can reach Dashboard when broker, subscription and activation match. | The valid-event path can write the card and complete its local transaction before GET reads the compatible store. | The bridge is conditional without a fixed global interleaving or observed visibility.
The consumer declares both exact event subscriptions. | Consumer run disables auto-commit and hooks up eachMessage to consumeMessage.
The per-topic payload and timestamp rules gate valid input. | Parse or validation failure inserts a rejected row, awaits explicit offset plus one, then returns.

The inbox duplicate commits and returns DUPLICATE before card SQL. | The place event writes only place fields; the forecast branch uses the strictly newer timestamp predicate, including the null-stored-timestamp alternative.

applyEvent begins a transaction, commits success or rolls back and rethrows on failure, and releases the client. | The caller awaits applyEvent before offset commit, so failed application bypasses the offset call.
Invalid parse or validation leads to rejection and explicit offset handling. | Validated input instead reaches applyEvent before its own offset call.
The duplicate path exits before card writes. | The strictly newer predicate and row-count result separate older/equal forecasts from applied forecasts.
The successful DB transaction completes before the separate offset commit. | A later offset failure can permit replay without a combined broker/DB atomic commit.
